papers.title: Allogeneic Bone Marrow Transplant for Inherited Metabolic Disorders
papers.summary: Rationale: Chemotherapy administration before a donor stem cell transplant is necessary to stop the patient's immune system from rejecting the donor's stem cells. When healthy stem cells from a donor are infused into the patient, the donor white blood cells can provide the missing enzyme that causes the metabolic disease. Sometimes the transplanted cells from a donor can make an immune response against the body's normal cells. Giving a monoclonal antibody, alemtuzumab, before transplant and cyclosporine and mycophenolate mofetil before and after transplant may stop this from happening. This ma

papers.title: A Clinical Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, and Initial Efficacy of JWK008 in Patients With Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I
papers.summary: This study is a single-center, single-arm, non-randomized, open-label, non controlled, dose-escalation, prospective clinical trial designed to assess the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of JWK008 injection in patients with MPS I.

papers.title: A Study of Intrathecal Enzyme Therapy for Cognitive Decline in MPS I
papers.summary:
This is a 24-month study of the use of laronidase administered into the spinal fluid to treat cognitive decline in mucopolysaccharidosis I (MPS I). MPS I is a rare genetic condition due to deficiency of the enzyme alpha-l-iduronidase. Laronidase is the manufactured form of the enzyme alpha-l-iduronidase.

MPS I is a heterogeneous disease with several clinical phenotypes ranging from the most severe, Hurler syndrome, to the attenuated forms, Hurler-Scheie and Scheie. Although patients with milder forms of MPS I may not have grossly observable problems with cognition, these patients do have lear

papers.title: Clinical Study of Aldurazyme in Patients With Mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS) I
papers.summary: This study is being conducted to demonstrate the safety and clinical efficacy of Aldurazyme treatment in MPS I patients

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of OTL-203 in Subjects With MPS-IH Compared With Standard of Care With Allogeneic HSCT
papers.summary: A multi-center randomized clinical trial to compare OTL-203 (gene therapy) with stem cell transplant (standard of care) in patients with MPS-IH (Hurler syndrome).

papers.title: Stem Cell Transplant w/Laronidase for Hurler
papers.summary: The investigators hypothesize that weekly infusions of Laronidase ERT for 10-12 weeks prior to transplant and 8 weeks following transplant will result in a reduction of glycosaminoglycans (GAG) burden that is associated with decreased complications following transplant.

papers.title: MT2013-31: Allo HCT for Metabolic Disorders and Severe Osteopetrosis
papers.summary: This single-institution, phase II study is designed to test the ability to achieve donor hematopoietic engraftment while maintaining low rates of transplant-related mortality (TRM) using busulfan- and fludarabine-based conditioning regimens with busulfan therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) for patients with various inherited metabolic disorders (IMD) and severe osteopetrosis (OP).

papers.title: An Extension Study of JR-171-101 Study in Patients With Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I (MPS I)
papers.summary: Phase I/II, open label, multicenter, multinational (Japan, Brazil and the US) extension study of JR-171-101 (NCT04227600) for the treatment of MPS I

papers.title: Gene Therapy With Modified Autologous Hematopoietic Stem Cells for the Treatment of Patients With Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I, Hurler Variant
papers.summary: This is a phase I/II study evaluating safety and efficacy of autologous hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells genetically modified with IDUA lentiviral vector encoding for the human α-L-iduronidase gene for the treatment of patients affected by Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I, Hurler variant

papers.title: Bone Marrow Transplant With Abatacept for Non-Malignant Diseases
papers.summary: This is a single arm, phase I study to assess the tolerability of abatacept when combined with cyclosporine and mycophenolate mofetil as graft versus host disease prophylaxis in children undergoing unrelated hematopoietic stem cell transplant for serious non-malignant diseases as well as to assess the immunological effects of abatacept. Participants will be followed for 2 years.

papers.title: A Study Investigating the Relationship Between the Development of Laronidase Antibody and Urinary GAG (Glycosaminoglycan) Levels in Aldurazyme® Treated Patients
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether the development of antibodies to laronidase in patients with MPS I receiving Aldurazyme® impairs the clearance of GAG substrate.

papers.title: Phase I/II Pilot Study of Mixed Chimerism to Treat Inherited Metabolic Disorders
papers.summary: The goal of this research study is to establish chimerism and avoid graft-versus-host-disease (GVHD) in patients with inherited metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Administration of IV Laronidase Post Bone Marrow Transplant in Hurler
papers.summary: This is a single center pilot study in which Laronidase will be given weekly for two years in patients with Hurler syndrome, also known as mucopolysaccharide IH (MPS I, Hurler syndrome), that have previously been treated with an allogeneic transplant.

papers.title: RGX-111 Gene Therapy in Patients With MPS I
papers.summary: RGX-111 is a gene therapy which is intended to deliver a functional copy of the α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) gene to the central nervous system. This is a safety and dose ranging study to determine whether RGX-111 is safe and tolerated by patients with MPS I.

papers.title: Effects of Adalimumab in Mucopolysaccharidosis Types I, II and VI
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to collect preliminary data on whether the drug adalimumab (also called Humira) can decrease pain and stiffness, improve quality of life, and is safe in people with mucopolysaccharidosis type I, II, or VI. In this study people will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will be treated with adalimumab the first 16 weeks of the study and then with a saline injection for the last 16 weeks of the study. The other group will start with the saline injection for 16 weeks and then switch to adalimumab for the last 16 weeks. The study subject and the study doc

papers.title: A Dose-optimization Study of Aldurazyme® (Laronidase) in Patients With Mucopolysaccharidosis I (MPS I) Disease
papers.summary: The main purpose of this study is to evaluate differences in the pharmacodynamic response of 4 Aldurazyme® (laronidase) dose regimens in patients with Mucopolysaccharidosis I (MPS I).

papers.title: Intrathecal Enzyme Replacement for Hurler Syndrome
papers.summary: This protocol will examine whether the enzyme alpha-L-iduronidase (Laronidase), delivered into the spinal fluid of patients with Hurler syndrome at intervals before and after bone marrow transplant, is a safe and effective approach to slow the neurologic degeneration seen in Hurler patients undergoing transplantation.

papers.title: Conditioning Regimen for Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem-Cell Transplantation
papers.summary: In this study, the investigators test 2 dose levels of thiotepa (5 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg) added to the backbone of targeted reduced dose IV busulfan, fludarabine and rabbit anti-thymocyte globulin (rATG) to determine the minimum effective dose required for reliable engraftment for subjects undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for non-malignant disease.

papers.title: Phase 3 Extension Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Aldurazyme® (Laronidase) in Mucopolysaccharidosis I (MPS I) Patients
papers.summary: This study is being conducted to collect additional long-term efficacy and safety data of Aldurazyme® (laronidase) patients with MPS I disease. Patients who were previously enrolled in the Phase 3 Double-Blind Study will be enrolled in this study.

papers.title: Extension Study of Intrathecal Enzyme Replacement Therapy for MPS I
papers.summary: This is a one-year extension study of the use of laronidase into the spinal fluid to treat spinal cord compression in mucopolysaccharidosis I. Mucopolysaccharidosis I is a rare genetic condition due to deficiency of the enzyme alpha-l-iduronidase. Spinal cord compression occurs in this condition due to accumulation of material called glycosaminoglycans (GAG). Laronidase is the manufactured form of the enzyme alpha-l-iduronidase that is deficient in mucopolysaccharidosis I patients. papers.title: Effects of Growth Hormone in Chronically Ill Children
papers.summary:
The specific aims for this study are -

1. To determine the effect of GH on height, height velocity, body weight and lean body mass. This specific aim tests the hypothesis that GH significantly improves height, height velocity, weight, weight velocity and lean body mass in chronically ill children who have grown poorly despite adequate nutritional rehabilitation.
2. To determine the effect of GH on whole body protein turnover (WBPT), IGF-1 levels and on cytokines. This specific aim tests the hypothesis that chronically ill children have increased catabolism, caused by high levels of circulatin

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for mucopolysaccharidosis type 1
Enzyme replacement with transferrin receptor-targeted α-L-iduronidase rescues brain pathology in mucopolysaccharidosis I mice.
papers.summary: Transferrin receptor-targeted IDUA fusion protein JR-171 delivered active enzyme across the blood-brain barrier, reduced brain and peripheral glycosaminoglycan accumulation, reversed established brain pathology, and preserved spatial learning in MPS I mice. Repeat-dose studies in cynomolgus monkeys found no test-agent-related toxicity through 40 mg/kg, providing nonclinical support for clinical evaluation in neuronopathic MPS I.

papers.title: Aptamer-based endocytosis of a lysosomal enzyme.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The paper develops transferrin-receptor-targeting aptamer conjugates to deliver alpha-L-iduronidase independently of the usual mannose or mannose 6-phosphate receptor pathways. A dephosphorylated alpha-L-iduronidase–aptamer conjugate entered alpha-L-iduronidase-deficient mouse fibroblasts through saturable, aptamer-dependent endocytosis and corrected lysosomal glycosaminoglycan accumulation.

papers.title: Treatment of the mouse model of mucopolysaccharidosis I with retrovirally transduced bone marrow.
papers.summary: In an Idua-/- mouse model of mucopolysaccharidosis I, transplantation of IDUA-transduced bone marrow generated variable alpha-L-iduronidase activity and corrected pathology in several peripheral tissues, with partial correction of brain pathology. Unmodified wild-type bone marrow reduced storage in liver and spleen but not in kidney or brain.

papers.title: Immune response hinders therapy for lysosomal storage diseases.
papers.summary: This commentary reports that anti-enzyme antibodies inhibit cellular uptake and limit the efficacy of alpha-L-iduronidase enzyme replacement therapy in a canine model of mucopolysaccharidosis I. It also reports that two months of oral cyclosporine A and azathioprine at ERT initiation induced immune tolerance and improved enzyme uptake in organs, suggesting that transient immunosuppression may enhance ERT for lysosomal storage diseases.

papers.title: Impaired bone remodeling and its correction by combination therapy in a mouse model of mucopolysaccharidosis-I.
papers.summary: In an Idua-deficient mouse model, IDUA deficiency was associated with high bone mass, pathological lysosomal storage in osteoblast-lineage cells, shortened bone-forming units, and reduced osteoclast numbers. Bone marrow transplantation from wild-type donors or its combination with enzyme replacement therapy corrected the bone-remodeling abnormalities, supporting evaluation of bone remodeling status in individuals with MPS-I.

papers.title: Guanidinylated Neomycin Conjugation Enhances Intranasal Enzyme Replacement in the Brain.
papers.summary: The study shows that guanidinylated-neomycin-conjugated IDUA (GNeo-IDUA), delivered intranasally, enters the mouse brain and reduces lysosomal storage, lysosomal abnormalities, and neurodegenerative astrogliosis in the IDUA-deficient mouse model of mucopolysaccharidosis I. The same delivery strategy also enhanced brain uptake and glycosaminoglycan clearance of sulfamidase in sulfamidase-deficient mice modeling mucopolysaccharidosis IIIA, while intravenous GNeo-IDUA reduced hepatic storage but did not affect the brain.

papers.title: Attenuation of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay enhances in vivo nonsense suppression.
papers.summary: In the Idua W392X knock-in mouse and patient-derived fibroblasts, attenuating nonsense-mediated mRNA decay with NMDI-1 increased mutant Idua transcript abundance and enhanced gentamicin-mediated nonsense suppression, restoring α-L-iduronidase activity and markedly reducing tissue glycosaminoglycan storage and secondary lysosomal enzyme elevations. NMDI-1 did not meaningfully reduce glycosaminoglycan storage alone and did not enhance NB84 in vivo, so the benefit was regimen- and readthrough-drug-dependent and was demonstrated primarily at biochemical rather than clinical endpoints.

papers.title: Substrate accumulation and extracellular matrix remodelling promote persistent upper airway disease in mucopolysaccharidosis patients on enzyme replacement therapy.
papers.summary: Adenotonsillar samples from ERT-treated mucopolysaccharidosis patients showed persistent lysosomal expansion, glycosaminoglycan accumulation, and extracellular matrix remodelling despite treatment. These structural changes, rather than a detectable primary inflammatory response, were associated with persistent upper-airway obstruction and indicate that ERT did not reverse established adenotonsillar storage pathology.

papers.title: Evaluation of non-reducing end pathologic glycosaminoglycan detection method for monitoring therapeutic response to enzyme replacement therapy in human mucopolysaccharidosis I.
papers.summary: In 10 people with mucopolysaccharidosis I receiving weekly intravenous recombinant human α-l-iduronidase, serum and cerebrospinal-fluid heparan sulfate non-reducing-end levels decreased substantially after treatment, while urine total glycosaminoglycans also decreased but retained a high background. The non-reducing-end assay was more specific for pathologic lysosomal glycosaminoglycan storage, but biochemical changes did not correlate significantly with changes in liver volume, spleen volume, or joint range of motion, and cerebrospinal-fluid levels did not normalize.

papers.title: Evaluation of AAV-mediated Gene Therapy for Central Nervous System Disease in Canine Mucopolysaccharidosis VII.
papers.summary: In naturally occurring canine MPS VII, intrathecal delivery of AAV9 or AAVrh10 vectors carrying canine GUSB cDNA produced widespread CNS GUSB activity, reduced glycosaminoglycan accumulation, and eliminated several markers of cortical secondary storage and inflammation. Intravenous delivery produced limited CNS enzyme activity and did not significantly reduce brain or spinal cord glycosaminoglycan accumulation, although it improved some disease markers and retained mobility in both treated dogs.

papers.title: Phenotypic Correction of Murine Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II by Engraftment of Ex Vivo Lentiviral Vector-Transduced Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells.
papers.summary: In an IDS-deficient mouse model of mucopolysaccharidosis type II, ex vivo transplantation of MNDU3-IDS lentiviral vector-transduced hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells produced supraphysiological circulating IDS activity, cross-corrected tissues, and reduced or normalized glycosaminoglycan accumulation. The intervention also improved CNS and skeletal outcomes, although glycosaminoglycan accumulation remained elevated in the spinal cord and LAMP-1 staining was not normalized in the aortic valve.

papers.title: A review of the clinical outcomes in idursulfase-treated and untreated Filipino patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type II: data from the local lysosomal storage disease registry.
papers.summary: This retrospective registry review reports that recombinant idursulfase enzyme replacement therapy in Filipino patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type II was associated with reduced glycosaminoglycan storage, improvement in several clinical endpoints, and fewer observed deaths than in untreated patients. The findings are limited by the small treated cohort, retrospective design, incomplete follow-up, absence of statistically significant comparisons, and the inability of idursulfase to cross the blood-brain barrier.

papers.title: Visual function restoration in a mouse model of Leber congenital amaurosis via therapeutic base editing.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that dual-AAV-delivered adenine base editing corrects the Rpe65 p.R44X nonsense mutation in retinal pigment epithelial cells of rd12 mice, a model of Leber congenital amaurosis. The treatment restored RPE65 expression, retinal electrical responses, and visual thresholds, supporting premature stop codon correction as a transferable strategy for nonsense variants.

papers.title: ABE8e adenine base editor precisely and efficiently corrects a recurrent COL7A1 nonsense mutation.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that ABE8e adenine base editing corrects the recurrent COL7A1 c.5047 C>T (p.Arg1683Ter) nonsense mutation in primary RDEB patient fibroblasts with 94.6% correction, restoring COL7A1 mRNA and collagen VII expression in fibroblasts and 3D human skin equivalents. Editing occurred without detectable off-target DNA editing or increased transcriptome-wide A-to-I changes, although dose-dependent bystander editing and limited testing of off-target sites were observed.

papers.title: Mini-dCas13X-mediated RNA editing restores dystrophin expression in a humanized mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that mini-dCas13X–mediated RNA base editing can convert pathogenic premature termination codons in DMD transcripts and restore dystrophin expression and muscle function in a humanized DMD mouse model. Local and systemic AAV delivery produced durable but tissue-dependent correction, while functional recovery was partial in some assays and bystander editing remained a safety limitation.

papers.title: Correction of human nonsense mutation via adenine base editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment in mouse.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that SpG adenine base editing can correct human dystrophin nonsense mutations through premature stop codon correction, restoring dystrophin in patient-derived cardiomyocytes and humanized DMD mice. Local or systemic AAV delivery produced mutation-dependent editing efficiencies and improved skeletal-muscle function, supporting adenine base editing as a potentially transferable strategy for nonsense variants in other monogenic diseases.

papers.title: Systematic empirical evaluation of individual base editing targets: Validating therapeutic targets in USH2A and comparison of methods.
papers.summary: The study establishes a transferable workflow for correcting nonsense variants by empirical base-editor and guide-RNA screening, followed by validation in endogenous cells and a humanized mouse retina. ABE8e delivered through split-intein AAV9 corrected the USH2A c.11864G>A p.(Trp3955*) variant, produced more than 50% productive editing, and restored USH2A expression and localization in treated retinal regions.

papers.title: Site-Specific RNA Editing of Stop Mutations in the CFTR mRNA of Human Bronchial Cultured Cells.
papers.summary: Sequence-specific RNA editing with REPAIRv2 and minixABE corrected CFTR premature UGA stop codons in human bronchial cells carrying W1282X or G542X, recovering partial full-length CFTR protein and increasing CFTR transcript levels. Recovery was incomplete, channel function was not established, and off-target editing and delivery remain important limitations.

papers.title: TMEM165 a new player in proteoglycan synthesis: loss of TMEM165 impairs elongation of chondroitin- and heparan-sulfate glycosaminoglycan chains of proteoglycans and triggers early chondrocyte differentiation and hypertrophy.
papers.summary: TMEM165 loss in pre-chondrogenic mouse ATDC5 cells, TMEM165-knockout HEK293 cells, and patient fibroblasts shortened chondroitin-sulfate and heparan-sulfate glycosaminoglycan chains, altered TGF-β/BMP signaling, and accelerated chondrocyte maturation and hypertrophy. Mn2+ supplementation restored glycosaminoglycan elongation and TGFβ/BMP signaling in TMEM165-deficient cells, but it was not tested for reversal of premature chondrocyte hypertrophy.

papers.title: Bone Growth Induction in Mucopolysaccharidosis IVA Mouse.
papers.summary: In a GALNS-knockout MPS IVA mouse model, one-time intravenous delivery of an AAV8 vector expressing the human NPPC/CNP peptide increased bone length, increased and reduced the size of growth-plate chondrocytes, improved some cartilage pathology, and reduced keratan sulfate accumulation in plasma and bone. The intervention did not improve gait, did not fully normalize chondrocyte pathology, had small sample sizes, and caused a mixed pattern of changes in bone morphometry and tissue glycosaminoglycans.

papers.title: SAG therapy restores bone growth and reduces enchondroma incidence in a model of skeletal chondrodysplasias caused by Ihh deficiency.
papers.summary: In an Ihh-deficient mouse model of skeletal chondrodysplasia, the smoothened agonist SAG restored hedgehog signaling in chondrocytes, rescued their proliferation and differentiation, improved skeletal growth and survival, and reduced enchondroma-like lesions. The study provides a transferable preclinical approach for directly correcting chondrocyte dysfunction, although efficacy was tested only in mice and primary mouse cells and occasional intestinal hyperplasia was observed.

papers.title: Correction of a knock-in mouse model of acrodysostosis with gene therapy using a rAAV9-CAG-human PRKAR1A vector.
papers.summary: The paper reports that intravenous rAAV9-CAG-human PRKAR1A gene therapy improved skeletal growth and restored growth-plate chondrocyte architecture in a PRKAR1A R368X knock-in mouse model of acrodysostosis. The treatment also corrected elevated urinary cAMP and improved kidney dysfunction, although limb bone length was not improved.

papers.title: Increased intracellular proteolysis reduces disease severity in an ER stress-associated dwarfism.
papers.summary: The paper shows that carbamazepine reduces disease severity in a mouse model of metaphyseal chondrodysplasia type Schmid by stimulating intracellular degradation of misfolded collagen X, reducing ER stress, and improving hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation and bone growth. The study provides a transferable experimental approach for disorders involving ER stress, intracellular accumulation of mutant structural proteins, and disrupted chondrocyte differentiation.

papers.title: Skeletal dysplasia-causing TRPV4 mutations suppress the hypertrophic differentiation of human iPSC-derived chondrocytes.
papers.summary: In CRISPR-Cas9-edited human iPSC-derived chondrocytes, the skeletal-dysplasia-causing TRPV4 V620I and T89I variants altered channel function and inhibited BMP4-induced hypertrophic differentiation relative to wildtype, with T89I generally producing the stronger inhibition. The study provides a human chondrocyte model and assays for measuring TRPV4-dependent calcium signaling, matrix production and mechanics, hypertrophy, and associated transcriptomic or protein changes.

papers.title: Myeloid/Microglial driven autologous hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy corrects a neuronopathic lysosomal disease.
papers.summary: In MPSIIIA mice, autologous hematopoietic stem cells transduced with a lentiviral vector expressing codon-optimized SGSH under the myeloid-specific CD11b promoter engrafted and produced higher brain SGSH activity than a PGK-driven vector. The CD11b strategy corrected hyperactive behavior, heparan sulfate accumulation, lysosomal abnormalities, neuroinflammation, and secondary GM2 ganglioside storage to near wild-type levels in most examined brain regions, while some regional inflammation and storage abnormalities remained.

papers.title: CRISPR-based gene editing enables <i>FOXP3</i> gene repair in IPEX patient cells.
papers.summary: In IPEX syndrome, site-specific CRISPR–Cas9 insertion of FOXP3 cDNA at the endogenous locus restored FOXP3 expression, improved regulatory T-cell suppression and effector T-cell proliferation control, and preserved HSPC differentiation and multilineage engraftment. The study provides an autologous ex vivo HSPC gene-correction precedent, but did not directly test IDUA correction or the IDUA-transduced hematopoietic stem cell engraftment mechanism in mucopolysaccharidosis type 1.

papers.title: Generation of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells with sickle cell mutation from induced pluripotent stem cell in serum-free system.
papers.summary: The paper reports that sickle cell anemia patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells can be differentiated in vitro into hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells and erythroid progenitors using a simple in-house serum-free medium. The generated cells expressed hematopoietic and erythroid markers and formed hematopoietic, including erythroid, colonies, but the study did not test IDUA-transduced hematopoietic stem cell engraftment or transplantation.

papers.title: Effects of vector backbone and pseudotype on lentiviral vector-mediated gene transfer: studies in infant ADA-deficient mice and rhesus monkeys.
papers.summary: The paper shows that lentiviral vectors carrying the ADA gene can deliver the therapeutic cDNA to multiple tissues and rescue the lethal phenotype and immune deficiency in ADA-deficient mice. HIV-1- and simian immunodeficiency virus-based vectors showed comparable biodistribution in rhesus monkeys, while pseudotype choice affected vector titer, copy number, and blood-cell transduction, supporting scale-up toward ADA-deficient severe combined immune deficiency treatment.

papers.title: A generic, flexible protocol for preimplantation human leukocyte antigen typing alone or in combination with a monogenic disease, for rapid case work-up and application.
papers.summary: The paper reports a rapid, flexible preimplantation HLA-typing protocol that can be combined with exclusion of a single-gene disorder before hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Across eight clinical cycles, genetic diagnosis was achieved for 94.7% of amplified biopsied blastomeres, and two healthy female infants were born; the study did not investigate IDUA-transduced hematopoietic stem cell engraftment.

unread.title: Evaluation of etanercept (a tumor necrosis factor alpha inhibitor) as an effective treatment for joint disease in mucopolysaccharidosis type I. A case report with whole-body magnetic resonance imaging.
unread.why: A MPS I case report provides direct patient data that etanercept reduced joint pain, improved walking and function, and reduced MRI-detected bone marrow edema.

unread.title: In vivo adenine base editing corrects newborn murine model of Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: The study directly demonstrates sustained in vivo correction of a common Idua mutation in a Hurler syndrome mouse model, reducing substrate storage and neurobehavioral deficits.

unread.title: Early Neonatal Cardiac Phenotype in Hurler Syndrome: Case Report and Literature Review.
unread.why: The case and review provide MPS I-specific early cardiac assessment and treatment data showing improvement after prompt ERT and HSCT.

unread.title: Effects of gentamicin inducing readthrough premature stop Codons: A study of alpha-L-iduronidase nonsense variants in COS-7 Cells.
unread.why: This study directly tests a therapeutic stop-codon readthrough approach for multiple disease-causing IDUA nonsense variants and demonstrates restoration of IDUA expression and activity in engineered cells.

unread.title: Long-term evolution of mucopolysaccharidosis type I in twins treated with enzyme replacement therapy plus hematopoietic stem cells transplantation.
unread.why: The report provides over seven years of MPS I-specific outcome data after combined ERT and HSCT, documenting stable development and symptom control.

unread.title: Treatment of latent tuberculosis in a child with mucopolysaccharidosis type I receiving enzyme replacement therapy: A case report.
unread.why: This case demonstrates a feasible concurrent treatment strategy for latent tuberculosis and MPS I receiving laronidase without serious adverse effects.

unread.title: Mucopolysaccharidoses types I and IIIA: Diagnosis and identification of novel polymorphisms associated with common mutations in Moroccan patients.
unread.why: The study establishes targeted molecular assays and sequencing methods for diagnosing MPS I and identifies the causal and potentially pathogenic variants in Moroccan families.

unread.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I in Mexico: Case-Based Review.
unread.why: This MPS I case reports clinical benefit from combined HSCT and ERT and illustrates sequencing-supported early diagnosis and management.

unread.title: Newborn Screening for Hurler Syndrome Facilitates Early Transplant and Good Outcomes.
unread.why: The cohort directly shows that newborn screening enables early cord-blood HCT with IDUA normalization, engraftment, and favorable developmental outcomes in Hurler syndrome.

unread.title: Laronidase for cardiopulmonary disease in Hurler syndrome 12 years after bone marrow transplantation.
unread.why: Reports use of laronidase and supportive ventilation with improved cardiopulmonary outcomes in a patient with severe MPS I.

unread.title: Intrathecal enzyme replacement for cognitive decline in mucopolysaccharidosis type I, a randomized, open-label, controlled pilot study.
unread.why: Directly tests intrathecal enzyme replacement in attenuated MPS I patients and provides cognitive clinical outcome data and safety findings.

unread.title: Lower Exposure to Busulfan Allows for Stable Engraftment of Donor Hematopoietic Stem Cells in Children with Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I: A Case Report of Four Patients.
unread.why: Reports a dosing and monitoring method that enabled stable donor engraftment with reduced toxicity in children with MPS I.

unread.title: Efficacy and safety of a biosimilar laronidase versus the reference laronidase in patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: Provides phase III evidence that a biosimilar laronidase has comparable efficacy and safety to reference laronidase in MPS I.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy in patients who have mucopolysaccharidosis I and are younger than 5 years: results of a multinational study of recombinant human alpha-L-iduronidase (laronidase).
unread.why: Multinational clinical trial data demonstrate laronidase safety and clinical benefit in young children with severe MPS I.

unread.title: Murine mucopolysaccharidosis type I: targeted disruption of the murine alpha-L-iduronidase gene.
unread.why: Describes a validated severe MPS I mouse model with biochemical, skeletal, facial, and lysosomal phenotypes suitable for treatment development.

unread.title: Prevention of neuropathology in the mouse model of Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: Demonstrates that a single AAV-IDUA injection delivers enzyme throughout the mouse brain and prevents neuropathologic changes in MPS I.

unread.title: Characterization of an MPS I-H knock-in mouse that carries a nonsense mutation analogous to the human IDUA-W402X mutation.
unread.why: This study develops and characterizes a genetically faithful mouse model that reproduces IDUA deficiency, GAG storage, skeletal abnormalities, and metabolic disease features for testing MPS I therapies.

unread.title: Identification and molecular characterization of alpha-L-iduronidase mutations present in mucopolysaccharidosis type I patients undergoing enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: In MPS I patients receiving enzyme replacement, the study links IDUA variants and fibroblast enzyme measurements to protein processing, disease severity, and immune response to therapy.

unread.title: Residual α-L-iduronidase activity in fibroblasts of mild to severe Mucopolysaccharidosis type I patients.
unread.why: A modified fluorogenic IDUA assay quantified very low residual activity and showed that it correlates with the clinical severity spectrum of MPS I.

unread.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis I mutations in Chinese patients: identification of 27 novel mutations and 6 cases involving prenatal diagnosis.
unread.why: The study applies targeted molecular genetic analysis to a large Chinese MPS I cohort and demonstrates its use for genotype characterization and prenatal diagnosis in six cases.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy with laronidase (Aldurazyme(®)) for treating mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: This systematic review reports randomized-trial evidence that weekly laronidase improves lung function, walking distance, and urinary GAG levels in patients with MPS I.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy with laronidase (Aldurazyme<sup>®</sup>) for treating mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: The updated systematic review confirms clinically measurable benefits and safety evidence for laronidase enzyme replacement in MPS I, including pulmonary, functional, and biochemical outcomes.

unread.title: A homology model for human alpha-l-iduronidase: insights into human disease.
unread.why: The paper constructs an IDUA homology model and uses it to rationalize how individual missense mutations cause severe or attenuated MPS I through distinct protein-folding effects.

unread.title: Outcome after three years of laronidase enzyme replacement therapy in a patient with Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: Three-year follow-up in an individual with severe Hurler syndrome provides concrete efficacy and limitation data for laronidase, including biochemical improvement but continued multisystem progression.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy with laronidase (Aldurazyme) for treating mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: This systematic review reports controlled-trial evidence that laronidase improves pulmonary function, exercise capacity, urinary glycosaminoglycan levels, hepatomegaly, and sleep-disordered breathing in MPS I.

unread.title: Valve surgery in a mucopolysaccharidosis type I patient: early prosthetic valve endocarditis.
unread.why: The report provides direct surgical experience and practical valve-selection and infection-prevention considerations for managing valvular disease in MPS I.

unread.title: Mucopolysaccharidoses Causing Valvular Heart Disease: Report and Review of Surgical Management.
unread.why: The report combines direct evidence of repeated valve replacement in Hurler-Scheie syndrome with a review of surgical management for MPS-associated valvular disease.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy with laronidase (Aldurazyme(®)) for treating mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: This review reports controlled-trial data showing that weekly laronidase improves functional, biochemical, and respiratory outcomes in MPS I.

unread.title: Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in a Case of Hurler-Scheie Syndrome Undergoing Enzyme Replacement Therapy.
unread.why: Bilateral deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty in a patient already receiving laronidase produced sustained visual recovery and clear corneal grafts.

unread.title: Synthesis and Evaluation of Novel Triaryl Derivatives with Readthrough-Inducing Activity.
unread.why: KY-516 was experimentally shown to suppress the IDUA Q70X premature stop codon and restore IDUA activity in mutant cells, providing a mutation-specific therapeutic candidate.

unread.title: Discovery of Novel Chromenopyridine Derivatives as Readthrough-Inducing Drugs.
unread.why: KY-640 increased IDUA activity and reduced glycosaminoglycan accumulation in Hurler patient-derived cells and also increased enzyme activity in mice.

unread.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I: The Importance of Early Diagnosis for Adequate Treatment.
unread.why: The case provides a concrete diagnostic pathway and clinical evidence for ERT and HSCT in a child with MPS I.

unread.title: Alterations in Hurler-Scheie Syndrome Revealed by Mass Spectrometry-Based Proteomics and Phosphoproteomics Analysis.
unread.why: The study provides a reusable patient-cell omics resource and identifies candidate protein and phosphorylation biomarkers in MPS IH/S.

unread.title: Clinical outcomes of exclusive enzyme therapy (laronidase) in a cohort of patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: A 48-patient longitudinal cohort provides direct evidence for laronidase efficacy across severe and attenuated MPS I and documents clinically useful outcomes.

unread.title: First-in-human intracisternal dosing of RGX-111 in severe MPS I is well tolerated and generates sustained neurodevelopment without HSCT.
unread.why: A first-in-human severe Hurler case reports tolerability and sustained neurodevelopmental outcomes from centrally administered IDUA gene therapy.

unread.title: Cognitive outcomes of a personalized stimulation protocol in Hurler-Scheie syndrome: A single-case study
unread.why: A six-week personalized stimulation intervention produced measured cognitive changes in a patient with Hurler-Scheie syndrome.

unread.title: RNA Activation of CEBPA in PBMCs Enhances α-L-Iduronidase Expression A Translational Adjuvant Therapy for MPS I After Bone Marrow Transplantation
unread.why: Cell, mouse, and human archival-sample data provide proof of concept for MTL-CEBPA as a post-transplant strategy to increase IDUA activity in MPS I.

unread.title: Metabolomic profiling in treated mucopolysaccharidosis IH reveals candidate biomarkers and adjunctive therapeutic pathways
unread.why: The study identifies treatment-associated metabolic signatures and 14 significantly differing metabolites that may serve as biomarkers or guides for adjunctive therapies in MPS I.

unread.title: Engineering Memory T Cells as a platform for Long-Term Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Lysosomal Storage Disorders
unread.why: Engineered memory T cells produced durable systemic IDUA activity and reduced glycosaminoglycan accumulation in an MPS I mouse model.

unread.title: Cardiac manifestations and effects of enzyme replacement therapy for over 10 years in adults with the attenuated form of mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: Reports long-term clinical cardiac outcomes and possible stabilization effects of enzyme replacement therapy in adults with attenuated MPS I.

unread.title: Long-term outcome of Hurler syndrome patients after hematopoietic cell transplantation: an international multicenter study.
unread.why: Provides multicenter long-term outcome data identifying predictors of success after hematopoietic cell transplantation in Hurler syndrome.

unread.title: The MPS I registry: design, methodology, and early findings of a global disease registry for monitoring patients with Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I.
unread.why: Describes a global disease registry and standardized assessment schedule for tracking MPS I phenotypes, treatments, and clinical outcomes.

unread.title: The clinical outcome of Hurler syndrome after stem cell transplantation.
unread.why: Reviews long-term clinical outcomes, limitations, and prognostic factors after stem cell transplantation in Hurler syndrome.

unread.title: Gentamicin-mediated suppression of Hurler syndrome stop mutations restores a low level of alpha-L-iduronidase activity and reduces lysosomal glycosaminoglycan accumulation.
unread.why: Shows experimentally that gentamicin suppresses IDUA stop mutations, restores low enzyme activity, and reduces lysosomal GAG accumulation in Hurler cells.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement in a canine model of Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: Demonstrates tissue distribution, antibody formation, and biochemical efficacy of recombinant IDUA enzyme replacement in a canine Hurler model.

unread.title: Can mucopolysaccharidosis type I disease severity be predicted based on a patient's genotype? A comprehensive review of the literature.
unread.why: Synthesizes genotype-phenotype data supporting predictive value of IDUA mutations, particularly biallelic nonsense variants, for MPS I severity.

unread.title: Combination of enzyme replacement and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation as therapy for Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: Reports clinical feasibility and short-term outcomes of combining peritransplant ERT with HSCT in children with Hurler syndrome.

unread.title: The future for treatment by bone marrow transplantation for adrenoleukodystrophy, metachromatic leukodystrophy, globoid cell leukodystrophy and Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: Reviews the established use of bone marrow transplantation in Hurler syndrome and related lysosomal storage diseases, with evidence for clinical and biochemical benefit.

unread.title: Whole exome sequencing unravels disease-causing genes in consanguineous families in Qatar.
unread.why: WES successfully identified the causal homozygous IDUA variant in a patient with Hurler syndrome, demonstrating a concrete diagnostic workflow.

unread.title: Haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) in combination with enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) in patients with Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: A multicenter study of 22 Hurler syndrome patients provides clinical data on combined ERT and HCT feasibility, tolerability, engraftment, and survival.

unread.title: Disordered breathing during sleep in patients with mucopolysaccharidoses.
unread.why: Objective sleep studies in children with MPS, including Hurler syndrome, were shown to be necessary for detecting, grading, and monitoring sleep apnea.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of enzyme replacement therapy in combination with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in Hurler syndrome.
unread.why: The trial reports safety, biochemical response, engraftment, and antibody findings for combined laronidase ERT and HSCT in Hurler syndrome.

unread.title: Musculoskeletal manifestations of Hurler syndrome: long-term follow-up after bone marrow transplantation.
unread.why: Long-term follow-up of seven successfully engrafted Hurler patients provides outcome data on the benefits and limitations of bone marrow transplantation.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in mucopolysaccharidosis type I using enzyme kinetics, immunoquantification and in vitro turnover studies.
unread.why: The study validates biochemical and cellular assays that distinguish residual enzyme activity and glycosaminoglycan turnover across MPS I phenotypes.

unread.title: Identification of mutations in the alpha-L-iduronidase gene (IDUA) that cause Hurler and Scheie syndromes.
unread.why: IDUA mutation identification and functional expression analysis provide diagnostic and genotype–phenotype methods for distinguishing Hurler and Scheie syndromes.

unread.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I: identification of common mutations that cause Hurler and Scheie syndromes in Japanese populations.
unread.why: Direct testing of common IDUA variants in Japanese patients established population-specific diagnostic markers associated with severe, intermediate, and mild MPS I phenotypes.

unread.title: Mutation analysis of 19 North American mucopolysaccharidosis type I patients: identification of two additional frequent mutations.
unread.why: The study validates a molecular testing approach and identifies two frequent IDUA mutations that improve mutation detection and prognostic genotype-phenotype prediction in MPS I.

unread.title: Analysis of five mutations in 20 mucopolysaccharidois type 1 patients: high prevalence of the W402X mutation. Mutations in brief no. 121. Online.
unread.why: Targeted screening of three IDUA mutations detected 80% of mutant alleles and 70% of patients in a Spanish MPS I cohort, constituting a concrete diagnostic assay.

unread.title: Molecular genetics of mucopolysaccharidosis type I: mutation analysis among the patients of the former Soviet Union.
Mucopolysaccharidosis type I: characterization of a common mutation that causes Hurler syndrome in Moroccan subjects.
unread.why: The data validate P533R as a high-frequency population-specific molecular marker and a targeted diagnostic approach for Moroccan Hurler syndrome.

unread.title: Urgent resection of a giant left atrial appendage aneurysm and mitral valve replacement in a complex case of Hurler-Scheie syndrome.
unread.why: This same-disease case report demonstrates successful surgical management of severe valvular and atrial complications in Hurler-Scheie syndrome.

unread.title: Impaired Hematopoiesis and Disrupted Monocyte/Macrophage Homeostasis in Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I Mice.
unread.why: Provides an MPS I mouse model with quantitative findings on hematopoietic stem-cell, progenitor, macrophage, calcium-signaling, phagocytosis, and apoptosis abnormalities.

unread.title: Evaluation and identification of IDUA gene mutations in Turkishpatients with mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: Reports molecular diagnosis of MPS I in Turkish patients by identifying IDUA variants and using segregation and computational analyses to assess pathogenicity.

unread.title: P-Tau and Subunit c Mitochondrial ATP Synthase Accumulation in the Central Nervous System of a Woman with Hurler-Scheie Syndrome Treated with Enzyme Replacement Therapy for 12 Years.
unread.why: Reports 12-year ERT outcomes in MPS I and identifies CNS p-Tau and SCMAS accumulation as potential disease-related biomarkers.

unread.title: Digital Microfluidics in Newborn Screening for Mucopolysaccharidoses: A Progress Report.
unread.why: Documents large-scale US newborn screening for MPS I using digital microfluidic IDUA activity measurement and follow-up classification of severe and attenuated cases.

unread.title: Genotypic and bioinformatic evaluation of the alpha-l-iduronidase gene and protein in patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type I from Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.
unread.why: Provides a regional IDUA mutation profile and computational structural models that improve molecular characterization and diagnosis of MPS I.

unread.title: Novel approach to idursulfase and laronidase desensitization in type 2 and type 1 S mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS).
unread.why: Reports a combined rapid and immunotherapy-like desensitization strategy that restored long-term tolerance to laronidase in an MPS I patient with severe hypersensitivity.

unread.title: 18-year follow-up of enzyme-replacement therapy in two siblings with attenuated mucopolysaccharidosis I.
unread.why: Provides long-term outcome data showing that early laronidase treatment can stabilize or improve multiple manifestations of attenuated MPS I.

unread.title: First Three Years' Experience of Mucopolysaccharidosis Type-I Newborn Screening in California.
unread.why: Reports California’s large-scale two-tier MPS I newborn screening program, including 1.3 million newborns screened and seven severe cases identified for early treatment.

unread.title: [Hurler syndrome: early diagnosis and treatment].
unread.why: Reports early biochemical and molecular diagnosis followed by laronidase and cord-blood transplantation, with observed cardiac, rhinologic, hepatomegaly, and cognitive outcomes.

unread.title: Implementation of an Affordable Method for MPS Diagnosis from Urine Screening to Enzymatic Confirmation: Results of a Pilot Study in Morocco.
unread.why: Establishes a low-cost diagnostic workflow for suspected MPS that confirmed 19 MPS I cases using urine substrate analysis followed by DBS enzyme testing.

unread.title: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography and in vivo confocal microscopy in cases of mucopolysaccharidosis.
unread.why: Demonstrates detailed corneal and anterior-segment imaging methods for quantifying structural abnormalities and deposits in MPS I.

unread.title: In silico analysis of potential off-target sites to gene editing for Mucopolysaccharidosis type I using the CRISPR/Cas9 system: Implications for population-specific treatments.
unread.why: The study provides an in silico method and off-target assay data for evaluating a CRISPR/Cas9 treatment strategy directly in MPS I.

unread.title: [Hurler syndrome. Early diagnosis and successful enzyme replacement therapy: a new therapeutic approach. Case report].
unread.why: This MPS I case reports clinical and biological improvement after laronidase treatment and supports early initiation of enzyme replacement.

unread.title: Longitudinal neurocognitive outcome in an adolescent with Hurler-Scheie syndrome.
unread.why: The paper supplies repeated longitudinal cognitive data in Hurler-Scheie syndrome that can inform natural-history monitoring and treatment evaluation.

unread.title: Chiari I malformation and syringomyelia in mucopolysaccharidosis type I (Hurler syndrome) treated with posterior fossa decompression: Case report and review of the literature.
unread.why: The study applies established urinary GAG and IDUA enzyme assays to diagnose and characterize a cohort of MPS I patients.

unread.title: Clinical features of Mexican patients with Mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: The study confirms MPS-I in patients using urinary GAG quantification and an α-L-iduronidase enzyme assay, providing directly reusable diagnostic approaches.

unread.title: Novel splice site IDUA gene mutation in Tunisian pedigrees with hurler syndrome.
unread.why: The paper combines patient sequencing with computational splice analysis to detect a pathogenic IDUA variant and support carrier and prenatal diagnosis.

unread.title: Surrogate Cerebrospinal Fluid Biomarkers for Assessing the Efficacy of Gene Therapy in Hurler Syndrome.
unread.why: Mass spectrometry and immunoblot validation identify four CSF protein candidates that track disease and response to AAV2/5-IDUA gene therapy in MPS I dogs.

unread.title: Case Report: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type I Treatment With α-L-Iduronidase Replacement Therapy.
unread.why: The report shows reduced urinary mucopolysaccharide levels and clinical improvement after laronidase treatment in a child with MPS I.
